title: Authorization fidelity harness with synthetic traffic and audit validation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a deterministic, repeatable harness that validates RBAC v2 permission semantics end-to-end under realistic traffic and SSO/SAML contexts, and asserts correctness in audit logs. This must catch regressions introduced by kernel-level permission shortcuts, routing fallbacks, and recent session-context changes. The harness will produce a set of canonical 'expectation vectors' (golden assertions) for role/resource combinations and a traffic replay engine that can run nightly and on-demand during PRs.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible suite of synthetic scenarios covering 90% of production role-resource permutations for the core product surface (generation, embedding, admin routes).
Each scenario emits an expected permission decision and a matching audit log entry; test fails if either differs from golden expectation.
Nightly CI job runs the harness and publishes a delta report to the security dashboard with failing vectors and implicated commits.
Support for SSO/SAML session attributes and group/role mappings; tests exercise mapped claims and fallback behavior.
Rollback guard: if a PR causes >1% of vectors to diverge, the PR pipeline flags it as blocking and notifies owners.
test_plan: Create synthetic user catalogs: internal_admins, org_admins, product_engineers, read_only_apps, automated_workers.
Generate API call patterns for each catalog: short synchronous gen, streaming chat, embedding batch, admin user-management endpoints.
Run permutations of role bindings, explicit denies, resource inheritance, and temporary grants; capture permission decisions from RBAC engine.
Record audit log entries produced by the platform for each request and normalize fields for comparison (actor, resource, action, outcome, request_id, session_claims).
Store canonical expectation vectors in a compact fixture format and version them alongside the harness; provide a PR-driven workflow to update goldens with signed approval.
runbook: Nightly CI: job 'rbac-fidelity-nightly' implemented in security-pipelines; failure artifacts archived to GCS and linked to the job.
If a delta appears: triage by running failing vector with --verbose to capture raw audit payloads; compare to previous golden with provided diff tool.
To update golden expectations: create PR with updated fixtures, include test rerun logs, add sign-off from security and product (labels: golden-update, security-approved).
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Initial spike complete. Prototype traffic generator that can synthesize SAML session claims and produce variety of request shapes.
2025-02-21: Added audit-normalizer module to strip non-deterministic fields (timestamps, ephemeral IDs) and canonicalize request signatures.
2025-03-04: Integrated harness with RBAC v2 sandbox endpoint; discovered mismatch in resource inheritance for delegated admin role (investigating fix).
2025-03-15: Defined acceptance gating thresholds and CI job spec. Began wiring nightly runner and notification channel to #sec-rbac-alerts.
2025-03-22: Completed SAML claim mapper tests and added coverage for group-to-role mapping edge cases.
decisions: Use event-driven diffing (compare normalized audit entries) rather than comparing raw logs to reduce flakiness from infrastructure metadata.
Store golden fixtures in a small compressed JSONL file per role-set to keep CI transfer costs low and make PR diffs reviewable.
Fail pipeline on >1% vector divergence; for lower deltas create an automated issue with attached debug bundle instead of blocking.
review_feedback: PM review (Marisol): prioritize admin-management endpoints and token-introspection routes in the first release.
Security review (Ravi): ensure audit-normalizer preserves cryptographic identifiers used for forensic correlation.
Design/UX (Lina): provide an easy-to-read delta report view in Console that groups failures by role and resource.
test_matrix_summary: Core roles: super_admin, org_admin, project_admin, developer, viewer.
Resource surfaces: api.generate, api.stream, api.embed, admin.users, admin.billing.
Decision dimensions: allow/deny, conditional grants (timeboxed), inherited bindings, group-mapped roles, explicit denies.
Environment axes: hosted API, dedicated vpool, private-vpc with SSO claims forwarded.
